### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c2ccf0bb6eee48bdc4961802e9951ec6d2283eb1` — the merge of head `640aed576dcfc7cd43e18b43c424296299124c51` into base `e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c2ccf0bb6eee48bdc4961802e9951ec6d2283eb1 && git checkout c2ccf0bb6eee48bdc4961802e9951ec6d2283eb1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9 640aed576dcfc7cd43e18b43c424296299124c51 && git checkout -B drift-repro e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9 && git merge --no-ff 640aed576dcfc7cd43e18b43c424296299124c51

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e84aeb36ce14169a633670f14ce8280fc998e2b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `640aed576dcfc7cd43e18b43c424296299124c51`
Local-runs: none

Delta review over the held `bb112188a9` record (the seat order `6106047492`, the dev report `6106372839`, the PR body as edited). The head is `bb112188a9` plus two commits: `e40ef1f1dc`, a merge of `origin/main` `e84aeb36ce`, and `640aed576d`, the patch-round-1 docblock rewrite. Net diff against `origin/main` (merge-base `e84aeb36ce`): the same 10 files, +788/-25. Every `bb112188a9` judgment is carried forward where the delta does not touch it; the delta is re-judged below.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head: 42, every one concluded — 38 success, 4 skipped, 0 failed, 0 cancelled. The skips: Console Pin Gate (path-scheduled; this diff removes nothing), Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), and one Auto Label plus one Check PR Size row from a second run of the PR-meta suite on the same head, each green in the other run; none of the four is a required context. All seven required contexts on `main` are green as named rows: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and its six shards), Dogfood Regression Gate (and its three shards), Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard.

Carried forward from `bb112188a9`, unchanged by the delta (per-file interdiff of the PR's change at the two heads, hunk headers ignored: identical for all nine non-spec files; the spec contract differs by the docblock hunk alone):
- `unstaffed?: boolean` on the `listRequests` filter, `countRequests` on the same parameter type — right.
- OR with `approverId`, confined to the two "who acts next" arms; AND with every other member; the alone case and `false` equals absent stated and right — right.
- `isOverrideActor` the only admin read, asked first with the caller's org (as `visibleRequestIds`) and per row with the row's org (as `attachViewers`); every added row `can_override: true`; the tenant wall holds; no path hands a member or an org-A tenant admin an org-B row — right.
- `slateNamesAPerson` behaviour-identical to the three inline copies; the in/out population true at the head; `team:NAME` literals do occur — right.
- Window `APPROVER_INDEX_CAP` with the same truncation warn as the approver index; a failed read throws; list and count share `awaitingRequestIds` — right.
- REST door: closed set, multiplicity set, `readDeclaredQueryBoolean` refusing everything but `true`/`false` as `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[0] { field: 'unstaffed', code: 'invalid_boolean' }` through `handleRouteError`, the `limit`/`offset` envelope; `invalid_boolean` in the ADR-0114 catalog — right.

Re-judged, the delta:
- The merge `e40ef1f1dc` — right, a conflict-free union. The head's merge-base with `main` is `e84aeb36ce` (the branch contains `main` whole). Between the two merge-bases, `main` moved `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` only through #22766 (an import line and three hunks near the payload display-target exposure read, about lines 56, 6391, 6419 and 6477); none of those hunks names or neighbours `awaitingRequestIds`, `unstaffedOverridableRequestIds`, `approverRequestIds`, `slateNamesAPerson`, `listRequests`, `countRequests`, `buildRequestWhere` or `isOverrideActor`. The PR's change in that file is byte-identical at both heads; the arm's code is as reviewed, with `APPROVER_INDEX_CAP = 10_000` now at line 6811. #22749, #22767 and #22736 touch no PR path. So the net diff at `640aed576d` equals the `bb112188a9` net diff plus the docblock delta, and nothing else.
- The new `limit` docblock sentence — true at the head, and complete for what it claims. Each clause checked against the code: "applied by the engine for every filter" — `listRequests` puts `limit`/`offset` on the engine `findOpts` after the id constraint and the visibility intersection, with no in-memory slice on the path; "a status array pushes down as `$in`" — `buildRequestWhere`; "the two arms first resolve to a bounded set of request ids: the approver index for `approverId`, the pending-request scan for `unstaffed`" — `awaitingRequestIds` over `approverRequestIds` (`sys_approval_approver`) and `unstaffedOverridableRequestIds` (`sys_approval_request`, `status: 'pending'`); "each within the implementation's id window (`APPROVER_INDEX_CAP`, 10,000 …, which warns when a probe reaches it)" — both probes read `limit: APPROVER_INDEX_CAP` and warn on `>= cap`; "the window then applies engine-side to the rows in that set" — `where.id` is the id or `$in` the set, then the engine window. The old sentence survives nowhere at the head (no generated artifact carried it; `check:generated` and the reference docs are green in CI). Pre-existing and outside the order, not a defect of this delta: the contract still does not say the implementation clamps `limit` to 1–200 (default 50) and serves unpaginated callers a 500-row window.
- Naming `APPROVER_INDEX_CAP` and its value in a spec contract docblock — a wording note, not blocking. The sentence attributes the bound to the implementation ("the implementation's id window … in `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`"), so it is not stated as a contract guarantee, and the file already names that package as the implementation (line 7); the seat's order asked for the constant by name, and the name and value are right at the head. The residual is drift: `check:spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` holds `path:NNN` citations, not bare identifiers, so a rename or re-tuning of the constant leaves this sentence stale with no gate reddening. A spelling that survives that — "an implementation-defined bound; the bundled `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` holds it at 10,000 at this release" — is the better one. Not owed by this round; the next change to the constant pays it.
- The PR body — right. One Acceptance-note edit, the line on the `limit` docblock, now saying it is corrected in this PR by `640aed576d`; no other line of the body changed (unified diff of the two bodies: that single line). The body's Suites and Gates sections still cite the `bb112188a9` measurements; the dev's report `6106372839` carries the `640aed576d` readings (spec suite, typecheck, `check:generated`, the plugin-approvals suite and the three dogfood approvals pins as the joint check for the merge). The check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts; the body's stale citation is not a false claim about the diff.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged from `bb112188a9`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest` at `minor` in `.changeset/22725-approvals-unstaffed-arm.md`; `@objectstack/dogfood` is private; `content/docs` is no package; `@objectstack/client`'s `src` does not move. Nothing moved is missing.
- The docblock rewrite is text inside a file already in the changeset's `@objectstack/spec` entry; it moves no accept set, so `minor` still fits and no changeset edit was owed (the order's own condition).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and the changeset — unchanged, matched; not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- No changeset line becomes false. The "How it composes" line ("paged server-side, and `total` counts both") now agrees with the contract's `limit` docblock instead of contradicting it; the "What it selects", "Who it returns them to", "What is refused" and "Before this" lines are judged true at the head as at `bb112188a9`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (c) the `limit` docblock, escalated at `bb112188a9`: resolved in-PR by `640aed576d`, as ordered — a text-only rewrite, no other contract text, no code, no changeset change. Answered.
- (a) `@objectstack/client` not widened: the seat's disposition stands — accepted as declared, no card. Answered; nothing at this head changes the reading (`packages/client/src/index.ts` hand-writes a filter without `q`, `limit`, `offset` or `unstaffed`, and no SDK consumer of the member is measured).
- (b) the rest boolean reader mirroring runtime's `parseBooleanParam`: the seat accepts it as written. Answered.
- The merge before the edit (`os-regen-merge.sh`, clean), the joint plugin-approvals and dogfood check beyond the order's gate list, the worktree recreated and removed: answered — procedural, and the per-file interdiff above is the review's own proof that the merge altered no PR path.
- The body's Suites/Gates sections citing `bb112188a9`: answered above — the order allowed one body edit, the current-head readings are in the report, and the head's check-runs are the verdicts.
- Writes this round as reported: `git push`, one PR-body patch, one report comment — within the order's budget. No governed surface in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard green); same-repo head.
